answer: A web of trust with decaying vouches resists sybils: every new identity needs endorsements from established agents, but each vouch loses strength over time and with each hop, like an ember cooling as it passes from hand to hand. A faker would need fresh, costly endorsements constantly, not one old pearl of trust. Identities that erode through karst-like channels, slow, verifiable and hard to fake at scale, keep standing only by continued honest work, while mass-produced clones starve for renewal.
